1: # Clean the order export
2: 
3: Our shop exports orders as a messy CSV (see `orders_raw.csv`). Write `clean.py` so that
4: 
5:     python3 clean.py INPUT.csv OUTPUT.csv
6: 
7: writes a clean CSV. It will be run on other exports with the same kinds of mess, so do not
8: hardcode anything about this particular file. Python 3.9, standard library only.
9: 
10: ## Input
11: - May start with a UTF-8 BOM. Blank lines and lines whose first character is `#` are ignored.
12: - Header names are matched after trimming, lowercasing and turning spaces into `_`
13:   (so ` Order ID` → `order_id`). Columns may come in any order. Extra columns are ignored.
14: - Columns: `order_id, customer_email, amount, currency, order_date, status, updated_at`.
15: - Every value may have surrounding whitespace; trim it.
16: 
17: ## Rules per field
18: - **order_id**: trimmed, uppercased. Rows with an empty order_id are dropped.
19: - **customer_email**: trimmed, lowercased. If it does not contain exactly one `@` with
20:   non-empty text on both sides, output an empty string (keep the row).
21: - **amount**: may contain a currency symbol (`$`, `€`, `£`) anywhere, spaces, thousands
22:   separators, and accounting negatives in parentheses: `(12.50)` = -12.50.
23:   Decimal separator rule: if both `.` and `,` appear, whichever appears **last** is the decimal
24:   separator and the other is a thousands separator. If only `,` appears and exactly two digits
25:   follow the last `,`, it is the decimal separator; otherwise `,` is a thousands separator.
26:   If only `.` appears it is the decimal separator.
27:   Output with exactly 2 decimals, rounding half away from zero (`2.005` → `2.01`).
28:   Rows with an empty or unparseable amount are dropped.
29: - **currency**: trimmed, uppercased. `$` → `USD`, `€` → `EUR`, `£` → `GBP`. If the currency
30:   field is empty, take it from a symbol in the amount; if there is none, use `USD`.
31: - **order_date**: output `YYYY-MM-DD`. Accepted inputs:
32:   `2026-03-04`, `2026/03/04`, `04.03.2026` (day.month.year), `03/04/2026` (month/day/year),
33:   `Mar 4, 2026` / `March 4, 2026`, `4 Mar 2026` / `4 March 2026` (English month names,
34:   any case). Single-digit day/month allowed in numeric forms. Rows with a missing or invalid
35:   date (e.g. `2026-02-30`) are dropped.
36: - **status**: trimmed, lowercased; `canceled` → `cancelled`. Allowed: `pending, paid, shipped,
37:   cancelled, refunded`. Anything else becomes `unknown`.
38: - **updated_at**: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` optionally followed by `Z`, or the same with a space
39:   instead of `T`. Only used for de-duplication; not in the output. Empty = oldest possible.
40: 
41: ## De-duplication
42: Rows with the same (normalised) order_id: keep only the one with the latest `updated_at`.
43: On a tie, keep the one that appears later in the file. Dropped rows (bad amount/date/id) never
44: take part in de-duplication.
45: 
46: ## Output
47: Header `order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status`, then rows sorted by
48: `order_date`, then `order_id`. Standard `csv` module quoting, `\n` line endings.

import csv
import io
import os
import subprocess
import sys

INPUT = "_test_in.csv"
OUTPUT = "_test_out.csv"

header = "Notes,Order ID, customer email ,amount,currency,order_date,status,UPDATED AT\n"

rows = [
    # amount forms and currency defaults
    ("A1", "<email>", "$1,234.50", "", "2026-03-04", "paid", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
    ("A2", "<email>", "1.234,56", "", "2026/03/04", "PAID", ""),
    ("A3", "<email>", "1.234.567,89", "eur", "04.03.2026", "canceled", "2026-01-01 00:00:00"),
    ("A4", "<email>", "1,234,567.89", "£", "03/04/2026", "shipped", ""),
    ("A5", "<email>", "€ 7,5", "", "Mar 4, 2026", "refunded", ""),
    ("A6", "<email>", "1,000", "", "March 4, 2026", "lost", ""),
    ("A7", "<email>", "(12.50)", "", "4 Mar 2026", "CANCELLED", ""),
    ("A8", "<email>", "(1,000.005)", "", "4 March 2026", "canceled", ""),
    ("A9", "<email>", "2.005", "", "2026-3-9", "pending", ""),
    ("A10", "<email>", ".5", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A11", "<email>", "12.", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A12", "<email>", "", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A13", "<email>", "abc", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A14", "<email>", "1.2.3", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A15", "<email>", "(12.50", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    ("A16", "<email>", "12.5", "", "2026-02-30", "pending", ""),
    ("A17", "<email>", "12.5", "", "2026-13-01", "pending", ""),
    ("A18", "bad@@x.com", "12.5", "", "Mar 4 2026", "pending", ""),
    ("A19", "<email>", "12.5", "", "Feb 29 2024", "pending", ""),
    ("A20", "<email>", "12.5", "", "Feb 29 2026", "pending", ""),
    ("", "<email>", "12.5", "", "2026-03-09", "pending", ""),
    # dedup: newer wins
    ("D1", "<email>", "10", "", "2026-03-01", "paid", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
    ("D1", "<email>", "20", "", "2026-03-02", "paid", "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z"),
    # dedup: later row wins tie
    ("D2", "<email>", "10", "", "2026-03-01", "paid", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
    ("D2", "<email>", "20", "", "2026-03-02", "paid", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
    # dedup: invalid later row does not replace
    ("D3", "<email>", "10", "", "2026-03-01", "paid", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
    ("D3", "<email>", "", "", "2026-03-03", "paid", "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z"),
    # dedup: empty updated is oldest
    ("D4", "<email>", "10", "", "2026-03-01", "paid", ""),
    ("D4", "<email>", "20", "", "2026-03-02", "paid", "1999-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
]

with open(INPUT, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    f.write("\ufeff")
    f.write(header)
    f.write("# a comment\n")
    f.write("\n")
    for order_id, email, amount, currency, order_date, status, updated in rows:
        out = io.StringIO()
        writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writerow(["note", order_id, email, amount, currency, order_date, status, updated])
        f.write(out.getvalue())

subprocess.run([sys.executable, "clean.py", INPUT, OUTPUT], check=True)

with open(OUTPUT, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    print(f.read())

os.remove(INPUT)
os.remove(OUTPUT)
